section_summary: The section completes a report on the South China Intelligence Group, describing its agents, locations, training, communications, financing and codes, then adds a September 1945 supplement on the organization in Canton. Later documents concern Hajimu Masuda’s citizenship, reported post-surrender Japanese activities in China, and Princess Sumair of Patiala. The Masuda correspondence includes three family relocation records.

subfiles.title: South China Intelligence Group, Five Provinces Information Department report, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Profiles South China Intelligence Group personnel and explains the group’s organization and operations.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages profile espionage, communications and propaganda agents, distinguishing reported members from suspects and listing their whereabouts. The report describes the group’s mission, recruitment, training, pay, cover stories, courier traffic, finances and codes for reporting Allied aircraft and troop movements. Its final pages chart personnel and Canton facilities.

subfiles.title: Supplementary information to Kweiyang X-2 report on South China Intelligence Group
subfiles.about: Adds information on the group’s control, leadership, facilities, training and surviving agents.
subfiles.summary: The supplement describes the group’s ties to the Nanking regime, Japanese funding, Canton headquarters and senior personnel. It identifies former chiefs and Japanese advisers, describes training and reporting practices, and notes agents believed to remain active or at liberty after Japan’s surrender.

subfiles.title: Request for information on Hajimu Masuda’s citizenship
subfiles.about: Requests Passport Division information needed to answer an SSU citizenship inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Neal asks Passport Division to supply the information requested by SSU.

subfiles.title: Strategic Services Unit inquiry about Hajimu Masuda
subfiles.from: Jason Paige Jr., Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State
subfiles.about: Seeks verification of Masuda’s claimed American citizenship after a report linked him to Japanese intelligence in Canton.
subfiles.summary: SSU requests a State Department file check of Masuda’s citizenship.

subfiles.title: Hajimu Masuda’s account of citizenship and wartime service
subfiles.about: Records Masuda’s statements about his birth, passport, Japanese citizenship and military service.
subfiles.summary: Masuda claims U.S. birth and citizenship despite involuntary Japanese military service and citizenship.

subfiles.title: Reply to SSU on Hajimu Masuda’s citizenship
subfiles.from: Jack D. Neal, Department of State
subfiles.to: Jason Paige Jr., Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.about: Relays Passport Division’s findings on Masuda’s passport and registration records.
subfiles.summary: Records confirm Masuda’s 1937 passport and 1939 renewal but contain no citizenship registration application.

subfiles.title: Passport Division findings on Hajimu Masuda
subfiles.about: Reports the passport record and absence of a citizenship registration application.
subfiles.summary: Passport Division confirms Masuda’s passport issuance and renewal; its file has no citizenship registration application.

subfiles.title: Transmission of report on post-surrender Japanese activities in China
subfiles.from: Jason Paige Jr., Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards an intelligence memorandum on Japanese activities after surrender.
subfiles.summary: Paige forwards the attached report to State and notes its distribution to intelligence offices.

subfiles.title: Post Surrender Japanese Activities in China
subfiles.about: Describes a reported Japanese underground organization and its activities in postwar China.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum traces the Ideological Center’s reported transformation into the National Salvation and Resurrection of the Motherland Center. It sets out the group’s beliefs, identifies members, and alleges propaganda, arms smuggling, attempted Soviet penetration and use of Japanese agents by Chinese organizations. Some individual allegations come from separately dated, evaluated reports.

subfiles.title: Transmission of memorandum on Princess Sumair of Patiala
subfiles.from: Jason Paige Jr., Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards information on Princess Sumair of Patiala.
subfiles.summary: Paige forwards the attached memorandum to State for information.

subfiles.title: Princess Sumair of Patiala
subfiles.about: Summarizes reports on Princess Sumair’s associates, finances and husband Morihiko Takami.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum recounts conflicting stories about Princess Sumair’s origins and describes her social circle in Paris and Shanghai. It alleges blackmail and property fraud, while describing Morihiko Takami’s wartime black-market activity and service as a Japanese naval intelligence informer. It also reports her current associates, passports and claimed ability to move money into Japan.
